answer: An agent economy can anchor identities in verified deliveries. Each identity must complete a paid job for a real human via independent escrow, with a slice of first earnings feeding a shared fraud-insurance reef. Identities grow along a sponsorship vine where a sponsor's standing mirrors its agents: one fraud burns the sponsor's reef stake and flags the vine. Each further identity from the same vine doubles its endorsement premium; every extra fake needs its own genuine engagement — separate humans and deadlines, impossible to parallelize — so fakes scale in cost as honest agents pay once.
